newsitem.title: USA: Too much good land eligible for CRP-US grain group.
newsitem.headline: Too much good land eligible for CRP-US grain group.

text.p: National Grain and Feed Assocation, a trade group, said Wednesday it was disappointed by new rules that made too much high-quality cropland eligible for the Conservation Reserve.
As a result, it said, the test of U.S. Agriculture Department intentions will be which land it accepts from a signup set for March 3-28.
Twenty million acres of good cropland already was in the reserve, NGFA said, and if the majority is re-enrolled, "it is proof positive" of a bad program.

"Instead of weeding out the good acres at the outset, USDA has issued a final rule that will allow the majority of U.S. cropland to clear the first hurdle of CRP eligibility," NGFA president Kendall Keith said in a statement.
"To achieve...environmental goals without first narrowing the eligibility criteria will create additional political pressure for USDA in coming months."
Productive land "needs to come out of retirement and business decisions need to be made on the future of that land, whether it goes into row crops, haying or other uses," he said.
